title: o11 vs. Composio Instant vs. Nevermined: Paid Tools for AI Agents
summary: Compare paid-tool access, connected accounts, setup effort, and execution evidence across o11, Composio Instant, and Nevermined.
body_markdown:
An agent that can write a research plan still needs access to search, page extraction, data, and perhaps a voice service to finish it. o11, Composio Instant, and Nevermined address that access problem: how to give an agent paid capabilities without making a developer establish a separate commercial relationship for every experiment.


The useful comparison is the path from a task to an authorized, usable result. Catalog breadth matters, but exact operations, account selection, spending enforcement, and recovery matter more once the agent starts working.


**Review date: October 18, 2026. Disclosure:** o11 publishes this article. This is a documentation and implementation review, not an independent performance benchmark. No paid supplier calls were made for this comparison. Product availability and account-specific terms must be checked before purchase.


## What you are actually buying


The OpenRouter analogy is useful because it describes a developer benefit: one integration can expose several suppliers. The analogy becomes less complete when tools perform different kinds of work. A search response, an image job, and a connected spreadsheet action have different inputs, ownership requirements, and completion conditions.


For a tool platform, evaluate three separate contracts. The capability contract says which operation exists and what it returns. The access contract says whose account supplies it and who is allowed to use it. The commercial contract says how a call is priced, authorized, and reconciled.


An attractive provider logo does not establish all three. A platform can support searching a provider’s public dataset without supporting its account administration. A generated video may be submitted successfully but remain unfinished. An operation can also exist in a catalog while requiring credentials that your workspace has not configured.


Start your shortlist with three tasks you intend to ship. For each, write the exact output and acceptance condition. This makes the comparison about removing work from your development process, rather than collecting a longer list of possible integrations. Our[guide to choosing an agent tool platform](https://o11.ai/blog/choose-ai-tool-platform) provides the broader evaluation framework.


## The current product shapes


Composio launched Instant on October 8, 2026. Its announcement describes wallet-funded core actions across more than 100 paid tools at launch, alongside connected applications. It states that connected customer accounts take precedence by default, that charges are visible, and that Instant actions cover core provider capabilities rather than every product setting. That makes Instant a direct alternative for buying tool access, not merely an OAuth connector.[Composio Instant announcement](https://composio.dev/blog/composio-instant) .


Nevermined’s catalog positions itself as a shared access point for paid services. Its October 15 update describes subscription credits usable across catalog services, readiness information, and router improvements including payment and delegation controls. Developers should assess its current catalog and credit access rather than assume that using it always means handling a cryptocurrency wallet themselves.[Nevermined product update](https://nevermined.ai/blog/whats-new-nevermined-subscriptions-catalog-readiness) .


o11’s inspected local implementation combines discovery, inspection, customer connections, wallet-funded execution, quotes, card-bound agent credentials, and persistent call status. Its local audit distinguishes implemented contracts from live supplier certification. Supplier accounts and funding require activation checks; a source catalog entry does not establish that a funded call is available today. Card funding is disabled in the inspected local configuration. These observations do not establish the state of a deployed service.


## A comparison you can use


Decision o11 implementation reviewed Composio Instant documentation Nevermined documentation


Main evaluation question Can this workspace discover and execute the required operation with explicit account and budget controls? Can the needed paid action run through Instant alongside existing connected apps? Can the catalog discover and purchase the needed service under the chosen access model?


Account model to inspect Customer connection or wallet-funded operation Connected provider account or Instant account Catalog service and selected buyer/payment access


Evidence required before launch Activated supplier account, usable rate, successful output, recovery path Exact Instant support, project access, policy, charge behavior Exact service readiness, current price, access mode, delivery behavior


Best pilot artifact Invocation record and accepted output Execution record with account source and reported charge Purchase/delivery evidence and accepted output


This table deliberately avoids checkmarks for broad claims such as reliability or security. Those labels conceal important details. An evaluation should ask whether a specific budget stops a specific request before supplier dispatch, or whether a specific revoked identity loses access to a specific account.


Ask each platform to demonstrate those behaviors in your own proposed workflow. A capability demonstrated in a vendor example is useful evidence about the product, but it is not a measurement of your account, model, region, or data.


## Spending controls need an enforcement boundary


There are several different controls commonly described as a budget. A tool allowlist restricts capabilities. A per-call maximum restricts one purchase. A cumulative allowance restricts a series of calls. An approval step asks a person about a particular action. A report tells you what already happened.


Composio’s Instant Tools documentation currently distinguishes these explicitly: it offers toolkit/tool policies and charge reporting, while a dollar cap per Session needs an application-side implementation. It also warns that a prepaid balance is not a hard cap because balance checks are asynchronous. That is a narrow, documented behavior, not a claim that Composio lacks controls altogether.[Instant Tools controls](https://docs.composio.dev/docs/instant-tools) .


For any platform, ask what happens when five calls are admitted together. If each reads the same remaining balance before the others update it, a sequential demonstration can look correct while concurrency overspends. The relevant test reserves the maximum permitted amount atomically before releasing a request to a supplier.


o11’s current source binds agent credentials to an active spending card and checks that card’s policy and allowance during authorization. Rotating a credential does not create a new allowance or reset history. Reservation checks support this implementation description; they do not prove a live supplier’s final charge or deployed availability. Nevermined publishes buyer budget and revocation controls in its catalog experience. The precise allowance, expiry, and delivery semantics still belong in your pilot.[Nevermined catalog](https://nevermined.ai/catalog/) .


## Existing accounts change the economics


A team that already buys search or media services may want to keep those contracts. Another team may need only a handful of calls during prototyping. Both can value a shared tool interface, but they are buying different kinds of convenience.


For existing accounts, check how the platform selects a connection. Can the same user connect a personal and a company account? Is selection explicit when they coexist? What happens when a connection expires? An automatic fallback to a funded platform account might keep a task moving, but it also changes who pays and potentially which resources the agent can see.


For platform-funded access, verify operation coverage and pricing units. A provider may offer a search endpoint directly but expose only a narrower lookup through a gateway. Some features require account-owned resources and cannot be treated as anonymous consumable requests.


Model the recurring workflow separately from occasional experiments. An existing provider commitment might make the recurring calls economical directly, while shared paid access remains useful for infrequent enrichment or new media capabilities. See[using your own accounts alongside pay-per-use tools](https://o11.ai/blog/provider-accounts-and-pay-per-use-tools) for the routing decisions a mixed setup needs.


## Compare completed workflows


Use a bounded company brief as a pilot. The agent must find official company information, retrieve two relevant pages, extract a fixed set of facts with citations, and produce a concise written result. Add audio only if it is an actual product requirement.


Freeze the input companies, model, prompt, time limit, and spending allowance. Define the acceptance rubric before seeing results. A brief can pass only if the required facts have supporting sources, the company identity is correct, and unsupported fields are marked unknown.


Record setup separately from runtime. The first trial includes account creation, authorization, configuration, and debugging. Later trials measure execution with access already configured. Combining the two hides whether a platform reduces initial friction or improves repeated operation.


Do not report only the cheapest successful run. Include unsuccessful calls, retries, time waiting for unresolved jobs, and human corrections. A service that returns a response quickly can still create downstream work if its output lacks provenance or the required fields.


Our[research-workflow cost protocol](https://o11.ai/blog/compare-research-workflow-costs) explains how to compare accepted briefs rather than isolated API prices. It also separates actual invoices from illustrative arithmetic, which is essential when a publisher sells one of the products being evaluated.


## Recovery is part of the integration


The difficult production case is often uncertainty. Your application submits a request, the connection times out, and you do not know whether the supplier accepted paid work. Retrying immediately can buy the same job twice.


Ask how the platform identifies the existing invocation and exposes supplier evidence. Can you recover a result using the original identifier? Does cancellation mean the queued job was removed, a stop request was sent, or actual work ended? Can an operator reconcile a call without submitting a new purchase?


For asynchronous services, inspect the entire path from submission to stored output. The result may become available after the initial agent turn ends. Download URLs may expire. A successful completion event can arrive more than once. These cases require durable application behavior, whether provided by the platform or built around it.


In o11’s reviewed implementation, an uncertain supplier outcome retains its hold for reconciliation and is not automatically purchased again. That is a design and local-audit statement. Apply the same question to every shortlisted alternative and record the evidence you receive rather than inferring behavior from a generic activity dashboard.


## When to shortlist each


Shortlist **Composio Instant** when the required paid actions overlap with Instant and your agent also needs connected workplace apps. Evaluate its account precedence and the application-side spending executor you would need for your particular budget rules.


Shortlist **Nevermined** when discovering and purchasing services through its catalog fits the workflow, especially when its available credit access and service readiness information match your operating requirements. Examine the exact delivery and allowance model for your chosen services.


Shortlist **o11** when you want a shared interface for inspecting tool contracts, choosing customer or wallet funding, and governing execution with scoped agent access. Treat activated supplier support, current rate evidence, and a verified first useful result as prerequisites. The implementation catalog alone is insufficient evidence of readiness.


Choose direct provider access for an operation when a special feature, negotiated contract, or resource ownership requirement is better served there. A platform need not own every call to remove meaningful setup work from the rest of the stack.


## Write the decision before you migrate


A useful decision memo fits on one page: the three required workflows; the operations each needs; the account and funding path; the measured setup burden; accepted-output rate; cost per accepted output; and unresolved recovery questions. Attach the actual pilot records.


Prefer the option with the smallest total burden for those tasks, provided it meets your hard requirements. Catalog size is a discovery aid. The purchasing decision rests on whether your agent can complete useful work, under the intended identity and allowance, with less setup and a recoverable execution path.


Revisit the memo when your workload changes. A prototype’s best access model can differ from a mature application’s, and a comparison reviewed in October 2026 will need fresh verification as these products evolve.
